findings.title: Cache status stays stale after deleting cached data
findings.body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop; it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. In the apps-installed calendar page `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` is rendered without an `onChanged` prop, so `onSuccess` is undefined. As a result the dropdown keeps showing "Cache Status / Last updated: …" and the "Delete cached data" entry after the rows were already deleted, until a full page reload. The sibling `disconnectMutation` in the same component does invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (and `viewer.apps.integrations`) in `onSettled`, so the omission looks accidental. Add the same invalidation to the deleteCache mutation.

findings.title: Cache deletion always fails for credentials not owned by the session user (delegation/team credentials)
findings.body: The authorization check is `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, i.e. it only accepts credentials whose `userId` equals the logged in user. Team/service-account delegation credentials are not user-owned (they are stored with `userId = null` and belong to a team / DelegationCredential), and in-memory delegation credentials even have negative ids, so the query never matches and the mutation throws "Credential not found or access denied". The UI does not guard against this: `canDisconnect` is computed from `delegationCredentialId`, but `hasCache` only checks the integration type, so the "Delete cached data" item is rendered for delegation-connected Google calendars and then always fails with the generic "Error deleting cache" toast. Either authorize team/delegation ownership in the handler or hide the action when `delegationCredentialId` is set. Note also that for in-memory delegation credentials, cache lookups are keyed by `userId` (see `getCachedAvailability`), so a delete-by-`credentialId` would not clear those rows even if it succeeded.

findings.title: Cache status reports expired cache rows as a live cache
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups over all CalendarCache rows for a credential without filtering on `expiresAt`. Expired rows are not removed from the table (availability reads just ignore rows with `expiresAt < now` and the row is only replaced on the next upsert), so a user whose Google cache expired weeks ago is shown "Cache Status — Last updated: <old date>" and offered "Delete cached data" even though the cache is effectively dead and the next availability request will miss. Add `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` to the `where` clause so the indicator reflects a usable cache. Relatedly, the migration backfills `updatedAt = NOW()` for all pre-existing rows, so after deploy every legacy cache row will display the deploy timestamp as its "last updated" time rather than when it was actually written.

findings.title: Unconditional bulk update of all SelectedCalendar rows on every cache refresh
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now ends with `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, whose only effect is to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` via the Prisma `@updatedAt` attribute (the data object is empty). This runs on every cache population, which is triggered by the Google push webhook — i.e. potentially many times per minute for busy calendars — and issues an UPDATE touching every SelectedCalendar row of the credential, adding write load and row-lock contention. The PR description itself notes that SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is not shown in the frontend (the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt), so this write has no consumer. Remove it, or make it conditional on an actual reader existing.

findings.title: Cache-status query bypasses the CalendarCache factory and runs on every connectedCalendars call
findings.body: The handler instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()` (the factory that returns the mock when calendar-cache is disabled / not enabled for the user's teams). Consequence: every `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` request — including onboarding, apps pages, and users/orgs where the calendar-cache feature is off — performs an extra `groupBy` aggregate over CalendarCache, even though the mock exists specifically to avoid that work when the feature is disabled. Scope the query (e.g. only for Google credentials, and via the repository factory) so non-cache users don't pay for it.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is macOS-only, so the script silently fails to update .env on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD/macOS in-place invocation. With GNU sed (Linux), the empty `''` argument is not consumed as an in-place suffix, so the command errors out and the file is never modified, yet the script still prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in $ENV_FILE to $TUNNEL_URL", leaving developers with a stale webhook URL while believing it was updated. Use a portable form (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E ... && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` or write to a temp file) and check the command's exit status before printing success. `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is also cwd-dependent and only correct when the script is run from `scripts/`.

findings.title: Unrelated dev:cron change introduces an undeclared `tsx` dependency invoked via npx
findings.body: Changing `dev:cron` from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` is unrelated to calendar cache status/actions and means the script depends on `tsx`, which is not declared anywhere in this package's devDependencies. On a clean checkout `npx` will download `tsx` from the network at run time (failing in offline sandboxes/CI) and pins nothing, so different developers may run different versions. Either revert this line or add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it through the package manager (`yarn tsx`).

findings.title: Removal of the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` assertion drops type-checking of the hand-written where clause
findings.body: `findMany` previously validated the hand-rolled `FindManyArgs` (whose `where` is a narrowed custom shape with e.g. `googleChannelId?: string | null | { not: null }`) against Prisma's generated `SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` via `satisfies`. The new code passes the raw object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany` without that assertion, so a future edit to the custom `FindManyArgs` type can now silently produce a filter Prisma will reject at runtime instead of failing the build. This change is also unrelated to the feature. Restore the `satisfies` assertion (or explain why it had to go) so the type contract keeps being enforced.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US locale
findings.body: The "cache_last_updated" value uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` while the component already uses `useLocale()` for translations. Non-US users therefore see US-formatted dates (M/D/YY, 12-hour clock) in an otherwise translated UI. Use the active user locale (e.g. from the locale context / `useLocale().i18n.language`) so the timestamp follows the user's locale settings.
